correctness.rationale: Uniform complex Haar coordinates have Dirichlet(1,1,1,1) law, with density 6. Inverse Walsh transform p_st=(1+sX+tY+stQ)/4 has absolute Jacobian 1/16; hence Q is uniform on [-1+|X+Y|, 1-|X-Y|]. Its conditional variance is (1-max(|X|,|Y|))^2/3 and E variance =2 Beta(2,4)=1/10. The Walsh contrasts X,Y,Q are pairwise orthogonal in L²; E Q²=1/5 by complex spherical fourth moments. Thus all commuting B have exact optimal nonlinear and affine risks |c3|²/10 and |c3|²/5. The proof covers all allowed parameters; a standalone exact-fraction script independently checked 3853 supplemental assertions and 200000 Haar Monte Carlo draws produced near-0.1 and near-0.2 risks (not a proof).

value.rationale: The lowest-dimensional noncollinear normal spectrum with a hidden commuting diagonal direction is the four-vertex planar parallelogram, not an arbitrary numerical slice. The theorem completely calculates the posterior distribution and sharp nonlinear-vs-affine Bayes risk for all such spectra and all commuting targets; the universally constant exactly 50% reduction is a meaningful finite-dimensional inference invariant beyond known qualitative sigma-algebra inclusion and marginal numerical-shadow density. It supplies a reproducible benchmark for operator-observation inverse problems, without requiring a downstream general theorem.
